questions.q: What does a Sequence Container do that a For Loop or Foreach Loop container does not?
options: It groups tasks into a subset control flow without repeating anything
It automatically parallelizes every task inside it
It converts child tasks into stored procedures
It requires an enumerator to function
questions.explain: Unlike the looping containers, a Sequence Container simply groups tasks and containers into their own control flow — it never repeats that flow.

questions.q: What happens when you set a Sequence Container's Disable property to True?
options: Every task and container inside it stops running, in one step
Only the first task inside it stops running
The container is permanently deleted from the package
Disable has no effect on tasks nested inside the container
questions.explain: Setting Disable on the container disables everything inside it at once — a fast way to isolate part of a package for debugging.

questions.q: How is a Sequence Container configured in SSIS Designer?
options: Through the Properties window — it has no custom editor dialog
Through a dedicated Sequence Container Editor dialog box
Only by editing the package's XML directly
Through the Foreach Loop Editor, using a special enumerator
questions.explain: The Sequence Container has no custom user interface; you configure it in the Properties window of SQL Server Data Tools, or programmatically.

questions.q: What happens to a variable defined inside a Sequence Container's scope?
options: It's visible only to the tasks and containers inside that Sequence Container
It automatically becomes visible to the entire package
It's deleted as soon as the container finishes running
It can only be read, never written, by tasks inside the container
questions.explain: A variable's scope follows where it's defined — a variable created inside a Sequence Container is limited to that container's tasks unless it's defined at package scope instead.

questions.q: Which of these is a genuine benefit of using a Sequence Container?
options: Setting a transaction attribute to commit or roll back everything inside it as one unit
Doubling the execution speed of every task inside it
Bypassing the need for connection managers
Automatically converting all child tasks to Execute SQL Tasks
questions.explain: A Sequence Container can have its own transaction attribute, letting you commit or roll back the work of everything inside it as a single unit — a more granular boundary than the whole package.
